assignments.reason: Tzedakah is a major causal node in this Torah, appearing as node1 in 5 eitza edges. It is the bridge between bitachon (trust) and dibbur (speech): bitachon enables tzedakah, and tzedakah produces the mouth/speech/adam. It is not identical in nature to either the intellect-domain (Package 1) or the speech-domain (Package 2) — it is an action (giving charity) that mediates between them. Along with bitachon, it forms a distinct functional cluster: the domain of righteous action enabled by trust.

Bitachon (trust in God) appears as both cause and effect in the causal chain: the intellect produces bitachon, and bitachon enables tzedakah. The text states explicitly 'עִקַּר הַצְּדָקָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַבִּטָּחוֹן.' Trust is the prerequisite disposition for charitable giving. Bitachon is not identical to the intellect itself (Package 1 covers the candle/sekhel domain), nor to speech (Package 2). It belongs with tzedakah as the disposition-and-action pair that mediates the Torah's causal flow.

The intellect (שכל) is the core concept of Package 1 (שֵׂכֶל וְנֵר הַדּוֹלֵק). In the eitza edges it appears as the cause of bitachon ('עִקַּר הַבִּטָּחוֹן בִּשְׁלֵמוּת הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׂכֶל'). The node חכמה is already the dominant node in Package 1 and שכל is its essential synonym in this Torah's context. Already covered by Package 1 nodes.

The lungs (ראה) are the physiological cause that enables the intellect: 'וְעִקַּר הַשֵּׂכֶל עַל יְדֵי הָרֵאָה.' While this is a causal relationship (lungs sustain moisture which sustains intellect), the lungs belong to the same physiological-metaphysical domain as Package 1's candle mechanism. The additions file already placed כרובים פורשי כנפים (the Cherubim-wings = lung-wings) in Package 1. The lungs are the physical substrate of the entire intellect-candle system.

This is a qualified form of ראה (lungs in their wholeness). It represents the same concept as ראה in its positive/complete state. The edge states 'כְּשֶׁהָרֵאָה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַבִּטָּחוֹן בִּשְׁלֵמוּת.' This is the lungs at their best — belonging to Package 1's domain of the intellect-sustaining physiological system.
This is bitachon in its complete form — a qualified version of בטחון. It belongs with the trust-and-charity cluster (new Package 4) as the ideal state of trust that enables perfect tzedakah.
Already assigned to Package 2 (אָדָם וְדִבּוּר). This eitza edge shows that tzedakah produces the adam-status, but adam's essential nature is speech — Package 2.
Already assigned to Package 2 via additions file. The 'definition of man' is the speech-faculty, which is the core of Package 2.
Already assigned to Package 2 (אָדָם וְדִבּוּר). Dibbur is the essential nature of man in this torah.
This is a resultative form of דבור — 'speech is made/formed.' It refers to the same essential concept as דבור in Package 2, just in its actualized form as the product of the causal chain.

This is a compound node: 'the mouth is formed, i.e., speech.' The text itself equates פה and דבור ('הפה דהינו הדבור'). Package 2 already contains אדם, דבור, and (via additions) פה and גדר אדם. This node is a direct alias of that cluster.

This compound node explicitly unites bitachon and tzedakah as a single causal condition: 'when one has trust and gives charity.' It is the composite state of the new Package 4 domain — trust-enabled righteous action.

This is the culminating result of the Torah's causal chain — the ability to transform mere chirping/sound into articulate speech. It describes the realized power of dibbur (Package 2). Its essential nature is the speech-faculty in its highest actualization. The Baal Shem Tov hearing words in the violin is the exemplar of this state.

new_packages.reason: Torah 225's causal chain runs: ראה → שכל → בטחון → צדקה → דבור/אדם. The intellect-domain (Package 1) and the speech-domain (Package 2) are already established. Between them sits a mediating cluster: trust in God (bitachon) and charitable giving (tzedakah). These two concepts are bound together by a tight reciprocal relationship: trust enables charity ('עִקַּר הַצְּדָקָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַבִּטָּחוֹן'), and together they form the practical-ethical action that bridges intellect and speech. They are neither aspects of the intellect itself nor aspects of speech itself — they are the moral-practical domain through which intellectual wholeness becomes actualized in the power of speech. This new package captures the Torah's central ethical teaching: that one needs trust to give, and giving creates the mouth.
